questions.question: How many types of emergencies are provided in the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Emergency (Article 352)**: This is proclaimed by the **President of India** when the security of the country or any part thereof is threatened by **war**, **external aggression**, or **armed rebellion**. It requires the written recommendation of the **Union Cabinet** and must be approved by **Parliament** within one month by a **special majority**.
 
• **State Emergency or President’s Rule (Article 356)**: This is imposed when the **President**, on receipt of a report from the **Governor** or otherwise, is satisfied that the state government cannot be carried on in accordance with the **Constitution**. It is also known as **Constitutional Emergency** and must be approved by Parliament within two months by a **simple majority**.
 
• **Financial Emergency (Article 360)**: The **President** can declare this if the **financial stability** or credit of India is threatened. While this provision exists to protect the national economy, it has **never been invoked** in the history of independent India, not even during the economic crisis of 1991.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part XVIII of the Constitution**:

 
 
• This part contains **Articles 352 to 360**, which outline the emergency provisions designed to safeguard the **sovereignty, unity, and integrity** of the nation.
 
• The **44th Amendment Act (1978)** introduced significant safeguards, such as replacing the term **'internal disturbance'** with **'armed rebellion'** for National Emergencies.
 
• During a **National Emergency**, the **Fundamental Rights** under **Article 19** are automatically suspended, and the President can suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of other rights, except **Articles 20 and 21**.
 
• Under **Article 356**, the **President** assumes the functions of the **State Government**, and the powers of the State Legislature are exercised by or under the authority of **Parliament**.
 
• The **38th Amendment Act (1975)** made the declaration of emergency non-justiciable, but this was subsequently reversed by the **44th Amendment Act**, allowing for **judicial review**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the permanent nature of the Rajya Sabha?

options.text: It can be dissolved by the President.
The Prime minister can dissolve it.
One-third of its members retire every two years.
It is dissolved every six years.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-third of its members retire every two years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rajya Sabha** is a **permanent body** according to the **Constitution of India** and is not subject to **dissolution** by the **President**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• There is no constitutional provision that grants the **Prime Minister** the authority to dissolve the **Council of States**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• To ensure legislative continuity as a **Continuing Chamber**, the law mandates that **one-third** of the total members of the house shall retire every **second year**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• While the **Lok Sabha** is dissolved every five years, the Rajya Sabha remains in existence, although its individual members serve a term of **six years**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Basis**:

 
 
• **Article 83(1)** explicitly states that the Council of States shall not be subject to dissolution, but nearly as may be, one-third of the members shall retire as soon as may be on the expiration of every second year.
 
• The **Representation of the People Act, 1951** further details the term of office for members of the Rajya Sabha as **six years**.
 
 
 
• **Leadership and Composition**:
 
 
• **Vice-President of India** is the **Ex-officio Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha, while a **Deputy Chairman** is elected from among its members.
 
• The maximum strength of the house is **250**, of which **12 members** are nominated by the **President** for their contributions to **Art, Literature, Science, and Social Service**.
 
• The remaining members are elected by the **Elected Members** of the **Legislative Assemblies** of the States and Union Territories through **Proportional Representation**.

• Female dancers traditionally wear the **Mekhela Chador**, a two-piece attire unique to the region, which is draped in a specific style to allow for the rhythmic and energetic movements of the dance.
 
• The **Mekhela** is a cylindrical cloth that is folded into pleats and tucked into the waist, while the **Chador** is a long fabric draped over the shoulder.

• Traditional accessories are essential to the performance, including **Assamese jewelry** such as **Gaam-Kharu** (broad bracelets), **Jonbir** (crescent-shaped necklace), and the **Kopou Phul** (foxtail orchid) placed in the hair.

questions.question: In what year was the German Expressionist artist group "Die Brücke" founded?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1905**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Die Brücke** (The Bridge) was a major group of **German Expressionist** artists formed on **June 7, 1905**, in the city of **Dresden**.
 
• The group was established by four architecture students at the **Dresden Technical University**: **Ernst Ludwig Kirchner**, **Fritz Bleyl**, **Erich Heckel**, and **Karl Schmidt-Rottluff**.
 
• The name was inspired by a passage from **Friedrich Nietzsche’s** 'Thus Spoke Zarathustra', symbolizing the artists' desire to serve as a bridge between the art of the past and the **modern avant-garde**.
 
• In **1906**, the group published a **manifesto** carved in wood, which declared their intent to achieve freedom of life and movement against established older forces.
 
• The artists are renowned for their **bold**, **non-naturalistic colors** and jagged, simplified forms that sought to convey powerful psychological and emotional states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Development and Membership**:

 
 
• Other significant artists joined the group later, including **Emil Nolde** and **Max Pechstein** in **1906**, and **Otto Mueller** in **1910**.
 
• The group shared a communal studio and developed a uniform collective style, heavily influenced by **Primitivism** and the **Post-Impressionism** of **Vincent van Gogh** and **Paul Gauguin**.
 
 
 
• **Relocation and Dissolution**:
 
 
• In **1911**, the members moved to **Berlin**, where their work began to reflect the alienation and frantic energy of the modern metropolis.

questions.question: If the star is similar to the Sun, what can be inferred about the exoplanet's surface temperature compared to Earth?

options.text: No effect of distance on temperature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Similar temperature**__.

 

__Key Points__

__
 
• The Sun is classified as a **G-type main-sequence star** (G2V), characterized by an effective surface temperature of approximately **5,778 K**. If an exoplanet orbits a star of the same spectral class, the **Stellar Luminosity** (total energy output) remains nearly identical to that of our Sun.
 
• Surface temperature is primarily governed by **Stellar Flux**, which follows the **Inverse Square Law**. This law states that the intensity of radiation is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source.
 
• For an exoplanet to have a **Similar temperature** to Earth, it must be located within the **Circumstellar Habitable Zone** (CHZ). In a solar analog system, this zone is situated at an **Orbital Radius** of roughly **1 Astronomical Unit (AU)**.
 
• At **1 AU** from a Sun-like star, a planet receives an **Insolation** (solar constant) of about **1,361 Watts per square meter**. If the exoplanet possesses an **Atmospheric Composition** and **Bond Albedo** (reflectivity) comparable to Earth, its **Radiative Equilibrium** will result in similar thermal conditions.

Additional Information__

 
• **Factors Affecting Planetary Temperature**:

 
 
• **Greenhouse Effect**: Even with similar stellar flux, a dense atmosphere rich in **Carbon Dioxide** or **Methane** can lead to extreme heating, as seen on **Venus**.
 
• **Albedo**: A planet with high ice cover reflects more **Shortwave Radiation**, potentially leading to a **Cooler** surface despite being in the habitable zone.
 
• **Stellar Classification**:
 
 
• **M-Dwarfs (Red Dwarfs)**: These are much cooler than the Sun; planets must orbit much closer to achieve Earth-like temperatures, often becoming **Tidally Locked**.
 
• **O or B Type Stars**: These are massive and hot, pushing the habitable zone much further out into the star system.
 
 
 
• **Stefan-Boltzmann Law**: This principle explains that the power radiated per unit area of a **Black Body** is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature, a critical factor in calculating **Planetary Equilibrium Temperature**.

questions.question: What causes the precession of the Earth's axis?

options.text: Gravitational pull of the Sun and Moon

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gravitational pull of the Sun and Moon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Earth is not a perfect sphere but an **oblate spheroid**, characterized by a distinct **equatorial bulge** caused by its rotation.
 
• **Axial precession**, also known as the precession of the equinoxes, is primarily caused by the **gravitational forces** of the **Moon** and the **Sun** acting upon this equatorial bulge.
 
• Because the Earth's rotational axis is tilted at an angle of approximately **23.5 degrees** relative to the **ecliptic plane** (the plane of Earth's orbit), the gravitational pull of these celestial bodies creates a **torque**.
 
• This torque attempts to pull the Earth's axis into a perpendicular orientation relative to the ecliptic, but due to the Earth's **angular momentum** (rotation), the axis instead precesses like a spinning top.
 
• The Earth's axis completes one full circle of precession approximately every **25,800 years**, causing the position of the **North Star** to change over long geological periods; for instance, **Vega** was the North Star around 12,000 BCE and will be again in roughly 12,000 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milankovitch Cycles**: Precession is a critical component of these cycles, which describe the collective effects of changes in the Earth's movements on its climate over thousands of years.

 
 
• **Obliquity**: Refers to the change in the angle of Earth's axial tilt, which varies between **22.1 and 24.5 degrees** over a 41,000-year cycle.
 
• **Eccentricity**: Describes the variation in the shape of Earth's orbit around the Sun, changing from nearly circular to slightly elliptical over 100,000-year intervals.
 
 
 
• **Solar Winds**: These are streams of **charged particles** (plasma) ejected from the Sun's upper atmosphere. While they cause **geomagnetic storms** and **auroras**, they have no significant impact on the mechanical orientation of Earth's axis.
 
• **Nutation**: This is a small, periodic 'wobbling' superimposed on the larger precessional motion, largely caused by the specific **tidal forces** and the 18.6-year cycle of the Moon's nodes.

According to the **BODMAS** rule, operations are performed in the order: Brackets (B), Of (O), Division (D), Multiplication (M), Addition (A), and Subtraction (S).

**Calculations:**

⇒ 94 − 38 + 28 + 33 ÷ 3 + 21 − 18

⇒ 94 − 38 + 28 + 11 + 21 − 18

BODMAS Rule

It defines the **precedence** of operators. Brackets are solved first, followed by 'Of' (multiplication), then Division, Multiplication, Addition, and finally Subtraction.

The 'Of' Operator

The term **Of** is treated as a high-priority multiplication that must be evaluated before the standard **Division** or **Multiplication** operators.

Grouping for Addition/Subtraction

To avoid **calculation errors**, always group all positive numbers together and all negative numbers together before performing the final subtraction.

questions.question: Which of the following is greater than (5/6)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **proper fractions** where the difference between the **numerator** and **denominator** is the same, the fraction with the **largest numerator** is the largest.

Check Gaps: (6 − 5) = 1, (4 − 3) = 1, (3 − 2) = 1, (11 − 10) = 1, (5 − 4) = 1.

Since all gaps are equal to 1, compare numerators: 10 > 5 > 4 > 3 > 2.

Therefore, 10/11 > 5/6.

**∴ The correct answer is 10/11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Base fraction = 5/6

**Formula Used:** Decimal Conversion Method

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/faab705adf6e3f1eac6ca3de8a2cf8ff3c6a755954b49ef7ac5d1afdf0ee921a.png] 

Convert each fraction into its **decimal equivalent**:

⇒ 5/6 = 5 ÷ 6 ≈ 0.833

⇒ 3/4 = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75

⇒ 2/3 = 2 ÷ 3 ≈ 0.666

⇒ 10/11 = 10 ÷ 11 ≈ 0.909

⇒ 4/5 = 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8

Comparing the values: 0.909 > 0.833

**∴ The correct answer is 10/11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Method

To compare a/b and c/d, compute (a × d) and (b × c). If a × d > b × c, then a/b > c/d.

Common Denominator Method

Convert all fractions to have the same **LCM** of denominators. The fraction with the largest numerator is then the greatest.

Fractions with Equal Numerators

If the **numerators** are the same, the fraction with the **smaller denominator** is the larger value (e.g., 3/5 > 3/7).

Square Root Decimal Rule

Multiplication of Decimals

questions.question: Area of a rhombus is 720 square cm. Side of the rhombus is 41 cm. What is the sum (in cm) of its diagonals?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **Rhombus**, the relation between side (a), Area (A), and sum of diagonals (S) is: S² = 4(a² + A).

⇒ S² = 4(41² + 720)

⇒ S² = 4(1681 + 720) = 4 × 2401

⇒ S = √(4 × 2401) = 2 × 49 = 98

**∴ The correct answer is 98 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Area** of rhombus = 720 cm², **Side** (a) = 41 cm.

**Formula:** **Area** = (d₁ × d₂)/2 | 4a² = d₁² + d₂²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4c21a99e9682bbeca8642fc8c1f83e0fc94bfc25a67b2feb90097c40a3e1801c.png] 

⇒ d₁ × d₂ = 2 × **Area** = 2 × 720 = 1440

⇒ d₁² + d₂² = 4 × **Side**² = 4 × 41² = 4 × 1681 = 6724

⇒ (d₁ + d₂)² = (d₁² + d₂²) + 2(d₁ × d₂)

⇒ (d₁ + d₂)² = 6724 + 2(1440) = 6724 + 2880 = 9604

⇒ d₁ + d₂ = √9604

⇒ d₁ + d₂ = 98 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 98 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

A **rhombus** is a quadrilateral with all four sides equal. Its **diagonals** bisect each other at 90° and also bisect the internal angles.

Perimeter and Area

Perimeter = 4 × side. **Area** can also be calculated as base × height if the altitude is known.

Diagonal Relation

The relationship between the side and the **diagonals** is derived from the Pythagoras theorem: Side = √[(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²].

questions.question: One angle of a parallelogram is 45 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of its adjacent angle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **parallelogram**, any two **adjacent angles** (consecutive angles) are **supplementary**.

Sum of **adjacent angles** = 180°

Given angle = 45°

**Adjacent angle** = 180° − 45° = 135°

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

One angle of the **parallelogram** = 45°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of **interior angles** on the same side of a **transversal** between **parallel lines** is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/841998dccbabbed4afd079537bdccd5820aec7158511de55291d18461e6ad822.png] 

In **parallelogram ABCD**, AB is parallel to DC and AD is parallel to BC.

Since AD || BC and AB is the transversal:

⇒ ∠A + ∠B = 180° (**Adjacent angles** property)

⇒ 45° + ∠B = 180°

⇒ ∠B = 180° − 45°

⇒ ∠B = 135°

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Opposite Angles of a Parallelogram

The **opposite angles** of a parallelogram are always equal (∠A = ∠C and ∠B = ∠D).

Sum of All Interior Angles

The total sum of all **internal angles** in any **quadrilateral**, including a parallelogram, is always 360°.

Diagonals of a Parallelogram

The **diagonals** of a parallelogram **bisect** each other, though they are not necessarily equal in length.

questions.question: What is the Least Common Multiple of 0.75 and (25/30)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert decimal and large fractions into **simplest fractions**: 0.75 = 3/4 and 25/30 = 5/6.

Apply the fraction formula: **LCM** = LCM of **Numerators** ÷ HCF of **Denominators**.

LCM(3, 5) = 15 and HCF(4, 6) = 2.

Result = 15/2.

**∴ The correct answer is 15/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First value = **0.75**, Second value = **25/30**.

**Formula Used:** LCM of Fractions = LCM(Numerators) ÷ HCF(Denominators)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59280aa65d87076ac808d1b98eaf61b1aa9f475ef61948332f2418ce44c3ca73.png] 

⇒ First, simplify **0.75**: 0.75 = 75/100 = 3/4.

⇒ Simplify **25/30**: Divide both numerator and denominator by 5 → 5/6.

⇒ Now, find the **LCM** of 3/4 and 5/6.

⇒ LCM of **Numerators** (3, 5) = 15.

⇒ HCF of **Denominators** (4, 6) = 2.

⇒ Final **LCM** = 15/2.

**∴ The correct answer is 15/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Fractions

To find the Highest Common Factor of fractions, use the formula: HCF = HCF(Numerators) ÷ LCM(Denominators).

Standard Form Requirement

Always convert fractions to their **simplest/standard form** (where numerator and denominator are co-prime) before applying LCM or HCF formulas.

LCM × HCF Rule

For any two numbers **a** and **b**, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **LCM** and **HCF**: a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b).

questions.question: The Highest Common Factor of two numbers is 12 and their Least Common Multiple is 180. The ratio of the numbers is 5 : 3. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The **ratio** of the numbers is 5 : 3. **Sum of ratio units** = 5 + 3 = 8 units. Since the **HCF** is the common factor for the ratio units, **Sum** = Total units × **HCF** = 8 × 12 = 96. **∴ The correct answer is 96.**

questions.question: If A percent of A is 676, then what is the value of A²?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**A%** of **A** is equivalent to **A² / 100**.

Given: A² / 100 = 676

**A²** = 676 × 100 = 67600

**∴ The correct answer is 67600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Percentage** value = A%

**Base** value = A

**Result** = 676

**Formula Used:**

Percentage result = (**Percentage** × **Base**) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/edb37807fe749f48fb9d0e9047bcec4ac72c3886bc6b9ff8f2da32a656cc04a6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ (A ÷ 100) × A = 676

⇒ (A × A) ÷ 100 = 676

⇒ A² ÷ 100 = 676

⇒ A² = 676 × 100

⇒ A² = 67600

**∴ The correct answer is 67600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Percentage Rule

To find **x%** of any quantity **y**, we use the formula (x × y) ÷ 100.

Square of a Number

The **square** of a number is the result of multiplying the number by itself (A × A = A²).

Perfect Squares

In this problem, 676 is the square of **26**, thus 67600 is the square of **260** (A = 260).

questions.question: If 20 percent of a number is 80, then what will be the 160 percent of that number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **unitary method** to compare the **percentages** directly.

Given that 20% corresponds to **80**.

1% will correspond to 80 ÷ 20 = **4**.

Therefore, 160% will correspond to 160 × 4 = **640**.

**∴ The correct answer is 640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**20%** of a number = **80**

**Formula Used:**

Required Value = (Given Value ÷ Given Percentage) × Required Percentage

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e57ac7696e86f3c68344e306d3741bffbe456fdc27c5aa88f18f137f1b202d0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the number be **x**.

⇒ 20% of **x** = 80

⇒ (20 ÷ 100) × **x** = 80

⇒ **x** = (80 × 100) ÷ 20

⇒ **x** = 4 × 100 = **400**

⇒ Now, find 160% of **400**:

⇒ 160% of 400 = (160 ÷ 100) × 400

⇒ 1.6 × 400 = **640**

**∴ The correct answer is 640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage to a fraction, divide the value by 100 and simplify. Example: 20% = 20/100 = 1/5.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change is calculated as (New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value × 100.

Successive Percentage Change

If a number changes by a% then b%, the net effective change is (a + b + (ab ÷ 100))%.

questions.question: A person sells an article at the profit of 30 percent. Cost price and selling price both are decreased by 40 percent. What will be the new profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If both **Cost Price (CP)** and **Selling Price (SP)** are increased or decreased by the same percentage (k%), the **ratio of SP to CP** remains constant.

Initial Profit = 30% ⇒ Ratio SP : CP = 130 : 100 = 1.3 : 1

Since both are decreased by 40%, the new ratio remains 1.3 : 1.

New Profit % = (Ratio − 1) × 100 = (1.3 − 1) × 100 = 30%.

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Profit Percentage** = 30%, Decrease in **CP** = 40%, Decrease in **SP** = 40%.

**Formula:** New Profit % = [(New SP − New CP) / New CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/445afefecdbc8cb13b072baa0d6084062f0ef71f8c58ff314c60dd9d4ff9c08b.png] 

⇒ Let original **CP** = 100

⇒ Original **SP** = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130

⇒ New **CP** = 100 − (40/100) × 100 = 60

⇒ New **SP** = 130 − (40/100) × 130 = 130 − 52 = 78

⇒ New Profit = 78 − 60 = 18

⇒ New Profit % = (18 / 60) × 100 = 3/10 × 100 = 30%

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 and Loss % = (Loss/CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.

Constant Ratio Property

When both numerator and denominator of a fraction (SP/CP) are multiplied or divided by the same non-zero constant (or changed by the same %), the value of the **ratio** remains the same.

Successive Percentage Change

If a value changes by a% and then by b%, the effective change is [a + b + (ab/100)]%.

questions.question: Cost price of 30 articles is Rs. 260. Selling price of 40 articles is Rs. 260. What is the profit/loss percentage? (Cost price of all the articles is same. Selling price of all the articles is same.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **total amount** (₹260) is the same, use the **quantity ratio**.

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** per article = Inverse of **Quantity**.

CP : SP = 40 : 30 = 4 : 3

**Loss** = 4 − 3 = 1 unit

**Loss Percentage** = (1 / 4) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Cost Price (CP)** of 30 articles = ₹260; **Selling Price (SP)** of 40 articles = ₹260.

**Formula Used:** **Loss Percentage** = [(CP − SP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1f5bf2ad5d5e4ad1b891937c0db5a61657d1cc9f744b9183393b4ed74888045.png] 

⇒ **CP per article** = 260 / 30 = ₹26/3

⇒ **SP per article** = 260 / 40 = ₹26/4

⇒ **Loss per article** = (26/3) − (26/4)

⇒ **Loss per article** = (104 − 78) / 12 = 26 / 12 = ₹13/6

⇒ **Loss %** = [(13/6) / (26/3)] × 100

⇒ **Loss %** = (13/6 × 3/26) × 100 = (1/2 × 1/2) × 100

⇒ **Loss %** = 1/4 × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss on Quantity

If **CP** of x articles = **SP** of y articles, then **Profit/Loss %** = (x − y) / y × 100. If the result is positive, it is a **profit**; if negative, it is a **loss**.

Basic CP and SP Relation

**Selling Price (SP)** = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss%) / 100. This formula helps calculate the final value when either CP or percentage is known.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

Gain % = [Error / (True Value − Error)] × 100. This is used when a dealer uses **less weight** than the actual weight mentioned.

questions.question: A, B and C working alone can complete a work in 14, 21 and 42 days respectively. In how many days A, B and C together can complete the same work?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Assume **Total Work** = LCM of (14, 21, 42) = **42 units**. Efficiency of **A** = 42 ÷ 14 = 3; **B** = 42 ÷ 21 = 2; **C** = 42 ÷ 42 = 1. Total efficiency of **(A + B + C)** = 3 + 2 + 1 = **6 units/day**. Time taken together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 42 ÷ 6 = **7 days**. **∴ The correct answer is 7 days.**

questions.question: 5 men can complete a work in 15 days. 6 women can complete the same work in 10 days. 4 boys can complete the same work in 12 days. 8 boys, 10 men and 12 women together can complete the same work in how many days?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Individual capacities: 1 man = 1/75, 1 woman = 1/60, 1 boy = 1/48.

Total daily work = (**10 men**/75) + (**12 women**/60) + (**8 boys**/48)

⇒ 2/15 + 1/5 + 1/6 = (4 + 6 + 5) / 30 = 15/30 = 1/2 of work per day.

Total time taken = 2 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time for **5 men** = 15 days ⇒ **1 man** = 75 days.

Time for **6 women** = 10 days ⇒ **1 woman** = 60 days.

Time for **4 boys** = 12 days ⇒ **1 boy** = 48 days.

**Formula Used:**

**Total Work = Efficiency × Time**

Total Work Equation

Total work remains constant and can be expressed as M₁D₁H₁ = M₂D₂H₂ where M is number of workers, D is days, and H is hours.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task (Efficiency = 1 ÷ Time).

Combined Work Formula

When multiple groups work together, their individual efficiencies (work done per day) are added to find the total work rate.

questions.question: Two trains are running in opposite direction with the same speed. Length of each train is 304 metres. They cross each other in 16 seconds. What is the speed (in m/s) of each train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **opposite direction**, Relative Speed = (Sum of Lengths) ÷ Time

Total distance = 304 + 304 = 608 m

Since **speeds are equal** (v), Relative Speed = v + v = 2v

2v = 608 ÷ 16 = 38 m/s

v = 38 ÷ 2 = 19 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 19 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of each **train** (L₁ = L₂) = 304 m

questions.question: Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice? The final report will have been completed by the research team before the board meeting begins.

options.text: The research team will complete the final report before the board meeting begins.
The research team will have completed the final report before the board meeting begins.
The research team completes the final report before the board meeting begins.
The research team has completed the final report before the board meeting begins.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The research team will have completed the final report before the board meeting begins**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the **Future Perfect Tense** structure. The passive formula for this tense is: **Subject + will + have + been + past participle (V3) + by + Agent**.
 
• In the given sentence, **the final report** is the subject receiving the action, **will have been completed** is the verb phrase, and **the research team** is the agent (doer of the action).
 
• To convert a **Future Perfect** sentence into the **Active Voice**, the agent of the passive sentence becomes the new subject, and the formula changes to: **Subject + will + have + past participle (V3) + Object**.
 
• Applying the conversion: The agent **the research team** moves to the subject position, the verb phrase changes from **will have been completed** to **will have completed**, and **the final report** becomes the direct object.
 
• The subordinate clause **before the board meeting begins** functions as an adverbial of time and remains unchanged in the transformation from passive to active voice.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Voice and Tense Consistency**:
 
 
• **Future Perfect Tense**: Used to indicate an action that will be completed at some point in the future before another action takes place. It is essential to maintain this tense during voice conversion.
 
• **Active Voice**: It is generally preferred in professional and academic writing because it is more direct, concise, and clearly identifies the **actor** performing the action.
 
• **Incorrect Tense Usage**:
 
 
• Option 1 uses **Simple Future** (will complete), which fails to capture the completed nature of the action relative to the deadline.
 
• Option 3 uses **Simple Present** (completes), which usually denotes facts, habits, or scheduled future events in a different context.
 
• Option 4 uses **Present Perfect** (has completed), which refers to an action finished in the past with current relevance, contradicting the future context of the sentence.
 
 
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice? The lights are to be switched off when you leave.

options.text: You will switch the lights off when you leave.
The lights should be switched off before leaving.
Switch off the lights when you leave.
Switched off the lights when you leave.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Switch off the lights when you leave**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence **'The lights are to be switched off when you leave'** is in the **passive voice**. It uses the **passive infinitive** structure, which consists of **'to be'** followed by the **past participle** (**'switched'**).

• This grammatical structure is commonly employed to state **rules**, **official instructions**, or **formal commands** where the actor is often implied rather than stated.

• To convert an instruction from passive to **active voice**, we generally use the **imperative mood**. In English, imperative sentences are inherently in the **active voice** because the subject **'you'** is understood as the performer of the action.

• An **imperative sentence** begins with the **base form** (infinitive without 'to') of the verb. Thus, **'to be switched off'** becomes **'Switch off'** in the active form.

• The phrase **'when you leave'** is a **subordinate clause** indicating time and remains unchanged in the conversion as it already identifies the actor (**'you'**).

• Therefore, the sentence **'Switch off the lights when you leave'** accurately captures the active voice while maintaining the original **imperative intent** and **temporal context**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Voice and Grammatical Mood**:

• **Active Voice**: The **subject** performs the action denoted by the verb. It is the most **direct** and **efficient** way to communicate instructions in everyday language.

• **Imperative Mood**: A verb mood used to give **orders**, **directions**, or **warnings**. It always utilizes the **present tense** and does not require an explicit subject because it is addressed to a second person.

• **Passive Voice**: Used when the **focus** is on the action or the **object** receiving the action (the **'lights'**) rather than the person performing it.

• **Incorrect Option Analysis**:

• **Option 1**: **'You will switch...'** uses the **future tense** (**'will'**), which changes the tone from a direct instruction to a statement about a future event or a prediction.

• **Option 2**: **'The lights should be switched off...'** incorporates the **modal verb** 'should' but maintains the **passive construction** (**'be switched'**), failing the requirement for active voice.

• **Option 4**: **'Switched off the lights...'** is grammatically flawed as an instruction because it uses the **past participle** or **past tense** form instead of the **base verb** required for an active imperative command.

</ul

• The adjective **nice** is followed by the preposition **to** when describing a person's **behavior** or **attitude** toward another person. 
• In the given sentence, the behavior of **Rakesh** is being directed toward **Radhika**, making **to** the grammatically correct choice. 
• Other adjectives that follow this same pattern (**Adjective + to + Someone**) include **kind**, **polite**, **rude**, and **generous**. • **Option 1: 'with'** is typically used to describe how someone handles objects or general situations (e.g., **nice with** his tools), or sometimes to describe general companionship, but **to** is the standard preposition for directed behavior.

options.text: antagonistic remarks only added fuel into the fire
ambiguous remarks only added fuel to the fire
assiduous remarks only added fuel for the fire

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ambiguous remarks only added fuel to the fire**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence requires an idiomatic correction and a contextual vocabulary improvement. The standard English idiom is **add fuel to the fire** (or **flame**), which means to cause a situation to become more **intense**, **excited**, or **uncontrollable**, typically in a negative way. The original phrase **added fuel in the fire** uses the incorrect preposition **in**.

• The word **ambitious** (showing a strong desire for success) does not logically contrast with the intention to **pacify** (to calm or soothe). In a **diplomatic context**, remarks that are **ambiguous** (vague or open to multiple interpretations) are a common cause of escalating **tensions** because they lead to **misunderstanding** and **mistrust**.

• Replacing **ambitious** with **ambiguous** creates a logical transition using the conjunction **but**, indicating that while the **diplomat** intended to resolve the conflict, the **lack of clarity** in his speech achieved the opposite result.

• Option 1 is incorrect because it uses the preposition **into**, which is not the standard form of the idiom, and **antagonistic** implies an intentional **hostility** that contradicts the **intended** goal of the speech.

• Option 3 is incorrect because **assiduous** means showing great care and **perseverance**; such remarks would unlikely result in the worsening of a situation.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Ambiguous**:

• Originates from the Latin **ambiguus**, meaning **doubtful**.

• Key characteristic: It describes a **statement** or **sign** that can be understood in more than one way, often leading to **confusion** in **negotiations** or **legal documents**.

• **Antagonistic**:

• Derived from **antagonismos** (Greek), meaning **struggle**.

• Key characteristic: Shows active **opposition** or **hostility** toward someone or something.

• **Assiduous**:

• Refers to a person or action showing **meticulous** attention and **constant** effort.

• Key characteristic: Highly valued in **academic** and **professional** settings for **thoroughness**.

• To bring **peace** to a state of **turmoil** or **war**.

• Core function: It is a **transitive verb** often used in **international relations** and **conflict resolution**.

</ul
